facts.text: Tyronza originally grew as a railroad town fueled by a lumber industry that logged old growth oak and cypress from the swampy region.
The Southern Tenant Farmers Union was founded in Tyronza in 1934 to help sharecroppers secure better prices and fairer treatment from landowners.
Tyronza was historically a hotbed for socialism and communism during the early twentieth century.
A museum in Tyronza, operated by Arkansas State University, highlights the history of the region and the organizing efforts of tenant farmers.
Tyronza is one of the oldest cities in Poinsett County, with its origins dating back to the late nineteenth century.
Tyronza has evolved from a farming and retail center into a bedroom community for residents who work in Jonesboro or Memphis.
